recommendation: Keep the audit as-is. Do not reintroduce Order/OrderResponse-specific guidance; any future ambiguity about order fulfillment status should be addressed in the active Workflow, Request, Task, or relevant domain request/event resources.
issue_request: FHIR-5304 was a Published, Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 OO ballot comment asking to clarify old Order page text that said clients could determine non-performance by searching for order resources with no matching responses. The final resolution says the work was applied in the Workflow Module because Task replaces Order.
initial_application: No Jira-keyed FHIR-5304 commit was found. Git history shows commit 16997a29cae89d6a31d09dabd782afdb0077b2e7 removed Order and OrderResponse source files and their active fhir.ini entries, including the challenged wording, as part of the workflow refactor.
additional_context: Duplicate FHIR-7391 repeated the same ballot comment and was resolved as Duplicate. Current build configuration lists ServiceRequest, NutritionOrder, and Task as active resources, while DiagnosticRequest, NutritionRequest, Order, and OrderResponse are removed-resource entries. Current Workflow/Task text describes Task-based workflow-state tracking and querying Tasks whose focus is the request of interest.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The misleading old Order/OrderResponse sentence is absent from current source, the named DSTU1 artifacts are out of active build scope, and Task.focus/Workflow guidance already addresses how fulfillment state is represented in the current specification.
